newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Ciampi warns against EMU delay.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Ciampi warns against EMU delay.

text.p: Italian Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said on Wednesday that a delay to EMU could endanger monetary union.
He told a hearing in the Senate (upper house) that he believed delay would be "dangerous because it could be the start of further delays and nothing more ever gets done."
Ciampi said a "global" decision should be taken in the spring of 1998 before the planned single currency starts in 1999.
He said there was a duty to respect to the maximum the parameters but that other factors also had to be considered.
"If tomorrow Germany should have a ratio between state debt and GDP of 3.2 percent, it will be said that Germany is out. That would be nonsense," he said.
"The criteria help to reach a judgment, but the judgment is global on the capacity of a country to be in Europe."
